items.title: Duffy Jackson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, October 17, 1995
items.q: Sweets was on the band and Marshall Royal was still there, all the great members were still there of that 60s era band.

ctx.x: Now, it seems like I read you sat in with Basie when you were just a kid.

Yeah, twelve years old. You know, and it’s ironic too because Don Lamond was substituting for Sonny Payne for that two week engagement at the Riverboat at the Empire State Building here years ago. That would have been almost, around 1966 or so. And it was the last set on a Thursday night and at that time they were still playing three or four sets for dancing, you know. And there weren’t really a lot of people there. And so Don Lamond leaned over to Basie and said, “Hey, how about letting Duffy play one?” You know…

think I fell down running to the drums or something, but I get there, and you know the first song I had to play was “Shiny Stockings.” And when it came to that point where I had to play what I had to play, I looked at Basie and he looked at me and I said, “Don’t worry, I think I know what I have to do this time.” And I got through the song, and he kept me up there for the last ten tunes of the night. And it was such a thrill. But what’s wild, I get an emergency phone call from Count Basie around four nights…
